title: Engineered lipid nanoparticles can safely and efficiently deliver plasmid DNA for hemophilia A gene therapy.
snippet: Non-viral gene therapy for genetic disorders like hemophilia A (HA) can overcome major limitations posed by viral gene therapy, including vector-induced host immune responses and the inability to administer repeated doses. title: Replicating vs. non-replicating RNA therapeutics: Mechanisms, trade-offs, and future directions.
snippet: RNA-based therapies are providing new ways to treat infections, cancer, and inherited diseases. These therapies fall into two broad categories: non-replicating RNAs, like messenger RNA, small interfering RNA (siRNA), and antisense oligonucleotides; and replicating RNAs, such as self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) and defective interfering (DI) RNAs.
